thread:
sarah: Customer (acme-inc) reports streaming responses dropping mid-event when their client sits behind an HTTP/2 reverse proxy. Final JSON is truncated and there is no finish_reason or terminal marker. Repro steps attached below.

sarah: example of what they receive (raw SSE lines copied):
```
data: {"id":"resp-9a3","object":"chat.completion.chunk","choices":[{"delta":{"content":"... and some text that ends abruptly"}}]

```

alex: Do they see any connection-level errors? timeout, RST, or FIN?

sarah: No explicit RST. Their proxy logs show a normal stream close from upstream. When we bypass the proxy (direct to our hosted endpoint) streaming completes fine. Only fails when proxy speaks http/2 to the client.

ravi: Is it reproduced with curl? Which flags?

sarah: They repro with `curl --http2 -N` against the proxy and see the cut. With `curl --http1.1 -N` through the same proxy the stream completes.

alex: Hmm. Could be the proxy aggregating/merging frames and closing before the final event is flushed to the client. Any known Envoy/nginx version?

sarah: They use Envoy 1.25 with default HTTP/2 config. Customer willing to try bypass config.

maria: Short-term workaround: ask them to force http/1.1 between client and proxy or disable http/2 upstream if possible. Also try reducing SSE event size to see if fragmentation pattern changes.

alex: I'll escalate to eng-runtime. Can someone try to reproduce with a minimal http/2 proxy (envoy/nghttp) and our SSE payload pattern? If reproducible we can add a perf/regression test.

ravi: I can repro locally with an http2 frontend + upstream keepalive toggles. Looks like when the proxy sends a connection close during an in-progress data chunk the trailing bytes get dropped on the client side causing the JSON body to be invalid and finish_reason never emitted. Will capture a tcpdump and provide a small repro.

sarah: Created internal ticket INF-7892 and shared customer trace. Customer accepted a temporary bypass to unblock.

ops-bot: Ticket INF-7892 created and assigned to eng-runtime.

alex: Thanks. Next steps: (1) ravi to upload pcap + minimal repro, (2) eng-runtime to triage for a possible server-side change to flush final event frames more aggressively and ensure graceful shutdown path writes final marker, (3) share recommended proxy configs/workarounds with customer. :thumbsup:

sarah: I'll keep the customer updated. Thanks all.
